messages.subject: Re: Can I download a file from the server?
parts:
The following worked for me.  myfile.txt is the file stored on the server.

 output$downloadSum = downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {  outputfile.txt },
    content = function(file) {    
        file.copy("myfile.txt", file)
    }
  )

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: Can I download a file from the server?
parts: If it's a static file, why do you need any sort of handler at all? I forget the thread on this group where Joe Cheng tipped me off to it (thanks again, Joe) but long story short, all you have to do is create a "www" subdirectory in the app directory, and put your file there. Then, if the file's full path is SOMETHING/www/myFile.csv, you can generate a valid link to it with a("myFile.csv").

Le jeudi 24 octobre 2013 18:30:46 UTC+2, Alex Bokov a écrit :
If it's a static file, why do you need any sort of handler at all? I forget the thread on this group where Joe Cheng tipped me off to it (thanks again, Joe) but long story short, all you have to do is create a "www" subdirectory in the app directory, and put your file there. Then, if the file's full path is SOMETHING/www/myFile.csv, you can generate a valid link to it with a("myFile.csv").
